sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ yuyudhire vīrāḥ kurupāṇḍavasomakāḥ pārthivāś ca mahābhāgā nānādeśasamāgatāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: How did they wage war, those heroes — the Kurus, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Somakas — and the high-fortuned kings gathered from many lands?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yathā yuyudhire vīrāḥ kurupāṇḍavasomakāḥ kurukṣetre tapaḥkṣetre śṛṇu tat pṛthivīpate
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: How those heroes — the Kurus, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Somakas — waged war upon Kurukṣetra, that field of austerities, hear it now, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: avatīrya kurukṣetraṃ pāṇḍavāḥ sahasomakāḥ kauravān abhyavartanta jigīṣanto mahābalāḥ
english: Descending upon Kurukṣetra, the Pāṇḍavas together with the Somakas, mighty in strength and eager for victory, advanced against the Kauravas.

sanskrit: vedādhyayanasaṃpannāḥ sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ āśaṃsanto jayaṃ yuddhe vadhaṃ vābhimukhā raṇe
english: All of them accomplished in Vedic study, all rejoicing in battle, they hoped for victory in the war, or else for death facing the foe in combat.

sanskrit: abhiyāya ca durdharṣāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya vāhinīm prāṅmukhāḥ paścime bhāge nyaviśanta sasainikāḥ
english: Having advanced against the unassailable army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, they encamped with their troops on the western side, their faces turned eastward.

sanskrit: samantapañcakād bāhyaṃ śibirāṇi sahasraśaḥ kārayām āsa vidhivat kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Outside Samantapañcaka, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī had encampments by the thousands raised according to due rule.

sanskrit: śūnyeva pṛthivī sarvā bālavṛddhāvaśeṣitā niraśvapuruṣā cāsīd rathakuñjaravarjitā
english: The whole earth seemed emptied, with only the young and the aged left behind; it was bereft of horses and of men, stripped of chariots and elephants.

sanskrit: yāvat tapati sūryo hi jambūdvīpasya maṇḍalam tāvad eva samāvṛttaṃ balaṃ pārthivasattama
english: As far as the sun shines upon the circle of Jambūdvīpa, over all that expanse was the host assembled, O best of kings.

sanskrit: ekasthāḥ sarvavarṇās te maṇḍalaṃ bahuyojanam paryākrāmanta deśāṃś ca nadīḥ śailān vanāni ca
english: Gathered in one place, men of every class, they overspread a circle many leagues across, covering regions, rivers, mountains, and forests.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhiro rājā sarveṣāṃ puruṣarṣabha ādideśa savāhānāṃ bhakṣyabhojyam anuttamam
english: To all of them, O bull among men, King Yudhiṣṭhira appointed, for them and their mounts, food and provisions of the finest kind.

sanskrit: saṃjñāś ca vividhās tās tās teṣāṃ cakre yudhiṣṭhiraḥ evaṃvādī veditavyaḥ pāṇḍaveyo 'yam ity uta
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira devised for them watchwords of various kinds: 'He who gives this sign is to be known as one of the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: abhijñānāni sarveṣāṃ saṃjñāś cābharaṇāni ca yojayām āsa kauravyo yuddhakāla upasthite
english: The Kaurava prince assigned to all of them tokens of recognition, signs, and emblems, now that the hour of battle had arrived.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā dhvajāgraṃ pārthānāṃ dhārtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ saha sarvair mahīpālaiḥ pratyavyūhata pāṇḍavān
english: Beholding the crests of the Pārthas' banners, the high-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with all the rulers of the earth, drew up his ranks against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani madhye nāgasahasrasya bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritam
english: With a white parasol held above his head, surrounded by his brothers in the midst of a thousand elephants —

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā duryodhanaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ sarve pāṇḍavasainikāḥ dadhmuḥ sarve mahāśaṅkhān bherīr jaghnuḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: beholding Duryodhana so arrayed, all the Pāṇḍava warriors, exultant, blew their great conches and beat their war-drums by the thousands.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭāṃ svāṃ senām abhivīkṣyātha pāṇḍavāḥ babhūvur hṛṣṭamanaso vāsudevaś ca vīryavān
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, looking upon their own exultant army, grew glad of heart, and so too did the valiant Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: tato yodhān harṣayantau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau dadhmatuḥ puruṣavyāghrau divyau śaṅkhau rathe sthitau
english: Then, gladdening their warriors, Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya, those two tigers among men, standing upon their chariot, blew their divine conches.

sanskrit: pāñcajanyasya nirghoṣaṃ devadattasya cobhayoḥ śrutvā savāhanā yodhāḥ śakṛnmūtraṃ prasusruvuḥ
english: Hearing the blast of both the Pāñcajanya and the Devadatta, the warriors together with their mounts let flow their dung and urine.

sanskrit: yathā siṃhasya nadataḥ svanaṃ śrutvetare mṛgāḥ traseyus tadvad evāsīd dhārtarāṣṭrabalaṃ tadā
english: As other beasts tremble at hearing the roar of a lion, even so was Dhṛtarāṣṭra's host stricken with fear in that hour.

sanskrit: udatiṣṭhad rajo bhaumaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana antardhīyata cādityaḥ sainyena rajasāvṛtaḥ
english: A cloud of earthly dust arose, so that nothing could be discerned; and the sun was hidden, veiled by the dust raised by the army.

sanskrit: vavarṣa cātra parjanyo māṃsaśoṇitavṛṣṭimān vyukṣan sarvāṇy anīkāni tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And there the cloud rained down a shower of flesh and blood, drenching all the ranks — a portent strange to behold.

sanskrit: vāyus tataḥ prādurabhūn nīcaiḥ śarkarakarṣaṇaḥ vinighnaṃs tāny anīkāni vidhamaṃś caiva tad rajaḥ
english: Then a low wind arose, driving gravel before it, buffeting those ranks and scattering that dust about.

sanskrit: ubhe sene tadā rājan yuddhāya mudite bhṛśam kurukṣetre sthite yatte sāgarakṣubhitopame
english: Both armies then, O king, exceedingly eager for battle, stood arrayed upon Kurukṣetra like two storm-tossed oceans.

sanskrit: tayos tu senayor āsīd adbhutaḥ sa samāgamaḥ yugānte samanuprāpte dvayoḥ sāgarayor iva
english: And the meeting of those two armies was a wondrous thing, like the clash of two oceans when the end of an age is come.

sanskrit: śūnyāsīt pṛthivī sarvā bālavṛddhāvaśeṣitā tena senāsamūhena samānītena kauravaiḥ
english: The whole earth was emptied, with only the young and the aged left behind, by reason of that vast host gathered together by the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tatas te samayaṃ cakruḥ kurupāṇḍavasomakāḥ dharmāṃś ca sthāpayām āsur yuddhānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then the Kurus, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Somakas made a covenant, and they established the rules of warfare, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: nivṛtte caiva no yuddhe prītiś ca syāt parasparam yathāpuraṃ yathāyogaṃ na ca syāc chalanaṃ punaḥ
english: 'When our war has ceased, let there be goodwill between us once more, as before and as is fitting, and let there be no further treachery.'

sanskrit: vācā yuddhe pravṛtte no vācaiva pratiyodhanam niṣkrāntaḥ pṛtanāmadhyān na hantavyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: 'When the fighting between us is waged with words, the answering also shall be only with words; one who has withdrawn from the midst of the host is on no account to be slain.'

sanskrit: rathī ca rathinā yodhyo gajena gajadhūrgataḥ aśvenāśvī padātiś ca padātenaiva bhārata
english: 'A chariot-warrior is to be fought by a chariot-warrior, one mounted on an elephant by an elephant, a horseman by a horseman, and a foot-soldier only by a foot-soldier, O Bhārata.'

sanskrit: yathāyogaṃ yathāvīryaṃ yathotsāhaṃ yathāvayaḥ samābhāṣya prahartavyaṃ na viśvaste na vihvale
english: 'According to fitness, prowess, ardor, and age, one shall strike only after first giving challenge — never one who trusts unguarded, never one who is in distress.'

sanskrit: pareṇa saha saṃyuktaḥ pramatto vimukhas tathā kṣīṇaśastro vivarmā ca na hantavyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: 'One engaged with another, one off his guard, one turned away, one whose weapons are spent, one without armor — none of these is on any account to be slain.'

sanskrit: na sūteṣu na dhuryeṣu na ca śastropanāyiṣu na bherīśaṅkhavādeṣu prahartavyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: 'Not against charioteers, not against draft-animals, not against those who carry weapons to the warriors, nor against those who sound the drums and conches, shall a blow ever be struck.'

sanskrit: evaṃ te samayaṃ kṛtvā kurupāṇḍavasomakāḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmuḥ prekṣamāṇāḥ parasparam
english: Having made this covenant, the Kurus, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Somakas fell into utter wonder as they gazed upon one another.

sanskrit: niviśya ca mahātmānas tatas te puruṣarṣabhāḥ hṛṣṭarūpāḥ sumanaso babhūvuḥ sahasainikāḥ
english: And having taken up their stations, those great-souled bulls among men became, with all their troops, of joyful aspect and of good cheer.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ pūrvāpare saṃdhye samīkṣya bhagavān ṛṣiḥ sarvavedavidāṃ śreṣṭho vyāsaḥ satyavatīsutaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, observing the twilights of dawn and dusk, the holy sage, foremost of all the knowers of the Vedas, Vyāsa the son of Satyavatī —

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati raṇe ghore bharatānāṃ pitāmahaḥ pratyakṣadarśī bhagavān bhūtabhavyabhaviṣyavit
english: the holy grandsire of the Bhāratas, who saw with his own eyes what should come to pass in the dreadful war, knower of past, present, and future —

sanskrit: vaicitravīryaṃ rājānaṃ sa rahasyaṃ bravīd idam śocantam ārtaṃ dhyāyantaṃ putrāṇām anayaṃ tadā
english: to King Vaicitravīrya, grieving, afflicted, brooding then upon the folly of his sons, he spoke this in secret.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca rājan parītakālās te putrāś cānye ca bhūmipāḥ te haniṣyanti saṃgrāme samāsādyetaretaram
english: Vyāsa said: O king, your sons and the other rulers of the earth have run out their allotted time; meeting one another in battle, they will slay each other.

sanskrit: teṣu kālaparīteṣu vinaśyatsu ca bhārata kālaparyāyam ājñāya mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: As they, whose time is spent, go to their ruin, O Bhārata, understand the turning of time, and do not set your mind to grief.

sanskrit: yadi tv icchasi saṃgrāme draṣṭum enaṃ viśāṃ pate cakṣur dadāni te hanta yuddham etan niśāmaya
english: Yet if you wish to behold this battle, O lord of the people, then look — I grant you sight; witness this war.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca na rocaye jñātivadhaṃ draṣṭuṃ brahmarṣisattama yuddham etat tv aśeṣeṇa śṛṇuyāṃ tava tejasā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I have no wish to look upon the slaughter of my kinsmen, O best of brahmin sages; yet by your power may I hear this war in its entirety.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasminn anicchati draṣṭuṃ saṃgrāmaṃ śrotum icchati varāṇām īśvaro dātā saṃjayāya varaṃ dadau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When he wished not to see the battle but desired to hear of it, the lord and bestower of boons granted a boon to Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca eṣa te saṃjayo rājan yuddham etad vadiṣyati etasya sarvaṃ saṃgrāme naparokṣaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Vyāsa said: This Saṃjaya of yours, O king, shall tell you of this war; nothing in the battle shall be hidden from his sight.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā saṃjayo rājan divyenaiṣa samanvitaḥ kathayiṣyati te yuddhaṃ sarvajñaś ca bhaviṣyati
english: Endowed with a divine eye, O king, this Saṃjaya will recount the war to you, and he shall become all-knowing.

sanskrit: prakāśaṃ vā rahasyaṃ vā rātrau vā yadi vā divā manasā cintitam api sarvaṃ vetsyati saṃjayaḥ
english: Whether open or secret, whether by night or by day, even what is conceived in the mind — all of it Saṃjaya will know.

sanskrit: nainaṃ śastrāṇi bhetsyanti nainaṃ bādhiṣyate śramaḥ gāvalgaṇir ayaṃ jīvan yuddhād asmād vimokṣyate
english: Weapons shall not pierce him, nor shall weariness afflict him; this son of Gavalgaṇa shall come forth alive from this war.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca kīrtim eteṣāṃ kurūṇāṃ bharatarṣabha pāṇḍavānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ prathayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
english: And I shall spread abroad the fame of these Kurus, O bull of the Bhāratas, and of all the Pāṇḍavas; grieve not.

sanskrit: diṣṭam etat purā caiva nātra śocitum arhasi na caiva śakyaṃ saṃyantuṃ yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: This was ordained of old; here you have no cause to grieve, nor can it be held back: where there is righteousness, there is victory.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā sa bhagavān kurūṇāṃ prapitāmahaḥ punar eva mahābāhuṃ dhṛtarāṣṭram uvāca ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the holy great-grandsire of the Kurus addressed the mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra once again.

sanskrit: iha yuddhe mahārāja bhaviṣyati mahān kṣayaḥ yathemāni nimittāni bhayāyādyopalakṣaye
english: In this war, O great king, there shall be a vast destruction, even as I now mark these omens that portend terror.

sanskrit: śyenā gṛdhrāś ca kākāś ca kaṅkāś ca sahitā balaiḥ saṃpatanti vanānteṣu samavāyāṃś ca kurvate
english: Hawks and vultures, crows and herons, gathered together with the armies, swoop down at the forest's edge and form their flocks.

sanskrit: atyugraṃ ca prapaśyanti yuddham ānandino dvijāḥ kravyādā bhakṣayiṣyanti māṃsāni gajavājinām
english: And the birds, rejoicing, foresee a most terrible battle; the flesh-eaters shall devour the flesh of elephants and horses.

sanskrit: khaṭākhaṭeti vāśanto bhairavaṃ bhayavedinaḥ kahvāḥ prayānti madhyena dakṣiṇām abhito diśam
english: Shrieking 'khaṭā, khaṭā' in dread, harbingers of fear, the cranes pass through the midst of the sky toward the southern quarter.

sanskrit: ubhe pūrvāpare saṃdhye nityaṃ paśyāmi bhārata udayāstamane sūryaṃ kabandhaiḥ parivāritam
english: At both twilights, of dawn and of dusk, I behold without fail, O Bhārata, the sun at its rising and its setting ringed about with headless trunks.

sanskrit: śvetalohitaparyantāḥ kṛṣṇagrīvāḥ savidyutaḥ trivarṇāḥ parighāḥ saṃdhau bhānum āvārayanty uta
english: Bordered with white and red, dark-necked, and charged with lightning, three-colored bars of cloud screen the sun at twilight.

sanskrit: jvalitārkendunakṣatraṃ nirviśeṣadinakṣapam ahorātraṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ tatkṣayāya bhaviṣyati
english: A day and a night I have beheld in which sun, moon, and stars all blazed alike, with no distinction between day and dark: this shall be for destruction.

sanskrit: alakṣyaḥ prabhayā hīnaḥ paurṇamāsīṃ ca kārttikīm candro 'bhūd agnivarṇaś ca samavarṇe nabhastale
english: On the full-moon night of Kārttika the moon was unseen, robbed of its radiance, the color of fire against a sky of one same hue.

sanskrit: svapsyanti nihatā vīrā bhūmim āvṛtya pārthivāḥ rājāno rājaputrāś ca śūrāḥ parighabāhavaḥ
english: Heroes shall sleep slain, kings covering the earth, sovereigns and princes, brave men whose arms are like iron bars.

sanskrit: antarikṣe varāhasya vṛṣadaṃśasya cobhayoḥ praṇādaṃ yudhyato rātrau raudraṃ nityaṃ pralakṣaye
english: In the sky, by night, I mark without ceasing the fierce clamor of a boar and a cat warring together.

sanskrit: devatāpratimāś cāpi kampanti ca hasanti ca vamanti rudhiraṃ cāsyaiḥ svidyanti prapatanti ca
english: The images of the gods, too, tremble and laugh, vomit blood from their mouths, sweat, and fall down.

sanskrit: anāhatā dundubhayaḥ praṇadanti viśāṃ pate ayuktāś ca pravartante kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: War-drums sound though none has struck them, O lord of the people, and the great chariots of the warriors roll forth though none has yoked them.

sanskrit: kokilāḥ śatapatrāś ca cāṣā bhāsāḥ śukās tathā sārasāś ca mayūrāś ca vāco muñcanti dāruṇāḥ
english: Cuckoos and woodpeckers, blue jays and vultures, parrots, cranes, and peacocks utter dreadful cries.

sanskrit: gṛhītaśastrābharaṇā varmiṇo vājipṛṣṭhagāḥ aruṇodayeṣu dṛśyante śataśaḥ śalabhavrajāḥ
english: At the reddening of dawn there appear by the hundreds swarms of locusts, as it were warriors bearing weapons and ornaments, armored and mounted upon horses' backs.

sanskrit: ubhe saṃdhye prakāśete diśāṃ dāhasamanvite āsīd rudhiravarṣaṃ ca asthivarṣaṃ ca bhārata
english: Both twilights blaze forth, attended by a burning of the quarters of the sky; and there fell a rain of blood and a rain of bones, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yā caiṣā viśrutā rājaṃs trailokye sādhusaṃmatā arundhatī tayāpy eṣa vasiṣṭhaḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtaḥ
english: And she who is renowned throughout the three worlds, esteemed by the virtuous, Arundhatī — even by her has Vasiṣṭha been set behind.

sanskrit: rohiṇīṃ pīḍayann eṣa sthito rājañ śanaiścaraḥ vyāvṛttaṃ lakṣma somasya bhaviṣyati mahad bhayam
english: Yonder stands Śanaiścara, O king, afflicting Rohiṇī; the mark upon the moon is turned awry: a great terror shall come to pass.

sanskrit: anabhre ca mahāghoraṃ stanitaṃ śrūyate 'niśam vāhanānāṃ ca rudatāṃ prapatanty aśrubindavaḥ
english: And from a cloudless sky a most dreadful thundering is heard without cease, and from the weeping draft-animals teardrops fall.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca kharā goṣu prajāyante ramante mātṛbhiḥ sutāḥ anārtavaṃ puṣpaphalaṃ darśayanti vane drumāḥ
english: Vyāsa said: Asses are born of cows, and sons take pleasure with their mothers; the trees in the forest put forth flower and fruit out of their season.

sanskrit: garbhiṇyo rājaputryaś ca janayanti vibhīṣaṇān kravyādān pakṣiṇaś caiva gomāyūn aparān mṛgān
english: Princesses heavy with child bring forth monstrous things — flesh-eating creatures and birds, jackals and beasts of other kinds.

sanskrit: triviṣāṇāś caturnetrāḥ pañcapādā dvimehanāḥ dviśīrṣāś ca dvipucchāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ paśavo 'śivāḥ
english: Ill-omened beasts are born, three-horned, four-eyed, five-footed, with two organs, two heads, two tails, and fanged.

sanskrit: jāyante vivṛtāsyāś ca vyāharanto 'śivā giraḥ tripadāḥ śikhinas tārkṣyāś caturdaṃṣṭrā viṣāṇinaḥ
english: They are born with gaping mouths, uttering inauspicious cries — three-footed, crested, eagle-like, four-fanged, and horned.

sanskrit: tathaivānyāś ca dṛśyante striyaś ca brahmavādinām vainateyān mayūrāṃś ca janayantyaḥ pure tava
english: And likewise are seen other women, even those of the reciters of the Veda, bringing forth eagles and peacocks within your city.

sanskrit: govatsaṃ vaḍavā sūte śvā sṛgālaṃ mahīpate krakarāñ śārikāś caiva śukāṃś cāśubhavādinaḥ
english: A mare gives birth to a calf, O lord of the earth, and a bitch to a jackal; partridges, mynahs, and parrots cry out words of ill omen.

sanskrit: striyaḥ kāś cit prajāyante catasraḥ pañca kanyakāḥ tā jātamātrā nṛtyanti gāyanti ca hasanti ca
english: Some women bring forth four or five daughters at a birth, and these, the very moment they are born, dance and sing and laugh.

sanskrit: pṛthagjanasya kuḍakāḥ stanapāḥ stenaveśmani nṛtyanti parigāyanti vedayanto mahad bhayam
english: The little ones of common folk, still at the breast, dance and sing aloud within the houses of thieves, foretelling a great terror.

sanskrit: pratimāś cālikhanty anye saśastrāḥ kālacoditāḥ anyonyam abhidhāvanti śiśavo daṇḍapāṇayaḥ uparundhanti kṛtvā ca nagarāṇi yuyutsavaḥ
english: Others, driven by fate, scrawl figures of armed men; and infants, cudgels in hand, rush at one another, and, eager to fight, fashion mock cities and lay siege to them.

sanskrit: padmotpalāni vṛkṣeṣu jāyante kumudāni ca viṣvagvātāś ca vānty ugrā rajo na vyupaśāmyati
english: Lotuses, blue lilies, and water-lilies spring up upon the trees; fierce winds blow from every side, and the dust never settles.

sanskrit: abhīkṣṇaṃ kampate bhūmir arkaṃ rāhus tathāgrasat śveto grahas tathā citrāṃ samatikramya tiṣṭhati
english: Again and again the earth quakes, and Rāhu has seized the sun; and a white planet, passing beyond Citrā, stands fixed.

sanskrit: abhāvaṃ hi viśeṣeṇa kurūṇāṃ pratipaśyati dhūmaketur mahāghoraḥ puṣyam ākramya tiṣṭhati
english: Most especially does it foretell the undoing of the Kurus, this comet of dreadful aspect, that has mounted Puṣya and there stands still.

sanskrit: senayor aśivaṃ ghoraṃ kariṣyati mahāgrahaḥ maghāsv aṅgārako vakraḥ śravaṇe ca bṛhaspatiḥ
english: A great planet shall work fearful ill upon both armies: Aṅgāraka stands retrograde in Maghā, and Bṛhaspati in Śravaṇa.
